newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan, Central America to forge alliance-report.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan, Central America to forge alliance-report.

text.p: Taiwan, trying to break free from the diplomatic isolation imposed by rival China, plans to set up an organisation linking the island to 13 central American and Caribbean nations, a newspaper said on Thursday.

The China Times quoted senior foreign ministry officials as saying Taiwan Foreign Minister John Chang would announce the establishment of a "strategic alliance" during a visit to central America in July.
The organisation would allow Taiwan to organise its aid to the region and help cement ties with the area, it said.

Most of Taiwan's 30 diplomatic allies are underdeveloped states in Africa and central America. Taiwan severed ties with the Bahamas in May after it learned the Caribbean nation was preparing to establish ties with Beijing.
The report did not name the countries that would join the alliance, but said Panama was unlikely to participate. The newspaper did not elaborate.
A ministry official in charge of central and south American affairs declined to comment, but said the ministry would hold a news conference later to explain the situation.
China, rivals with Taiwan since a civil war split them in 1949, regards the island as a renegade province that one day must be reunified under mainland sovereignty.
Communist China says the Nationalist-ruled island is not eligible to join major international organisations and warns other countries against forging ties with the island.
Taiwan argues the island's 21 million people deserve to have a say in the international arena.

Local media have said Chang's trip to the region was aimed at countering China's attempts to woo allies and at paving the way for President Lee Teng-hui's trip to attend an international conference in Panama from September 7-10.
Lee has accepted an invitation to attend a conference for Panama Canal Zone users, giving him a rare opportunity to meet world leaders.
The Commercial Times said Taiwan's business leaders planned to form a large trade and investment delegation to visit central America with Lee in September.
